content: Positioning-technology comparisons (Zapworks guide 2026, ExpoFP Aug 2026, Navigine, Mappedin) agree: QR-code and NFC/RFID give point-fix localisation only, accuracy is limited to anchor point locations, there is no continuous tracking, accuracy depends entirely on code placement, and codes can be damaged, removed or obscured; maintenance is very low and setup is hours rather than days-to-weeks. BLE beacons give 1-3 m (ExpoFP: 2-5 m) continuous accuracy but need hardware, batteries and days-to-weeks of setup; Wi-Fi/UWB need infrastructure and a live connection and do not work offline. Indoor GPS degrades to 30-100 m. Conclusion for QR design: the honest product claim is point-to-point wayfinding from scanned anchors, which is exactly what ExpoFP and Navigine market, and it must never be described as real-time tracking.
